title: Bernie Sanders Urges Permanent Superintelligence Ban
source_used: Newsmax text as carried by Yahoo; International Business Times (Singapore edition)
key_facts: Senator Bernie Sanders, independent of Vermont, called on Monday 12 Oct in a post on X for a permanent ban on artificial superintelligence and an immediate pause in advanced AI development.

He was answering Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, who said last week on Politico's 'Decoded' podcast that society would have to accept 'some fairly severe cyber incidents' from open AI models in exchange for the freedom they bring.
Sanders wrote 'No, Mr. Altman. We won't accept a severe AI cyberattack in exchange for liberty' and 'The creators of any AI model, open-source or not, are not above the law'.
He raised hypothetical attacks on banks, hospitals, power grids and nuclear plants; International Business Times notes these were scenarios he posed, not incidents.

Sanders and Representative Greg Casar, a Texas Democrat, introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act on 23 Sep (Senate) and 24 Sep (House); it would create a Cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence and set prison terms of up to 20 years.
The bill has not become law (International Business Times).
Newsmax says President Trump has set up a 'Super Intelligence Force' and promotes AI development as a national priority.
quote_evidence: 'No, Mr. Altman. We won't accept a severe AI cyberattack in exchange for 'liberty,'' Sanders wrote.
'We must PAUSE advanced AI and permanently BAN artificial superintelligence before it is too late.'
Altman said society would have to accept 'some fairly severe cyber incidents' in exchange for the freedom such technology provides.
why_it_matters_hint: A senator uses a CEO's remark about accepting cyber incidents to press for his superintelligence ban bill.
event_date: Sanders' post: Monday 12 Oct 2026; Altman's podcast remark: the week before.
notes: Newsmax page blocked here (HTTP 000); the Newsmax text was read on its Yahoo copy, and the International Business Times Singapore edition (https://www.ibtimes.sg/should-we-accept-another-chernobyl-bernie-sanders-demands-ai-ban-after-sam-altmans-cyberattack-95085) confirms the post and the bill. Altman's remark was not carried in our earlier editions. Our 8 and 11 Oct editions carried earlier Sanders calls for a pause and for prosecuting AI chiefs. Post dated 12 Oct, before the window, so FOLLOW-UP and score lowered by 1.
